LayerNorm’s default affine scale is 1 and bias 0, making its output approximately unit variance when input variance exceeds epsilon. Thus, adding an unscaled normalized text vector can overwhelm small-initialized ID embeddings. Implementation inference: use `e(i)=ID(i)+α·σ_ID·LN(text(i))`, where `σ_ID` matches the supplied ID initialization and `α` controls initial text strength; apply any backbone embedding multiplier consistently after addition. Keep padding outputs zero after projection/normalization. This scaling is a design hypothesis, not an established optimum. [PyTorch LayerNorm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.modules.normalization.LayerNorm.html)

For text pooling, `EmbeddingBag(mode='mean', padding_idx=...)` avoids materializing the full item-by-token-by-dimension embedding tensor. For repeated item occurrences, deduplicate requested IDs within each forward pass, encode their token bags once, then gather with inverse indices; indexing preserves gradients and accumulates contributions from repeated uses. Reuse these differentiable representations across history and target lookups within that forward when practical. Deduplicating item requests should preserve repeated words inside each item’s text. [EmbeddingBag](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.sparse.EmbeddingBag.html), [torch.unique](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.unique.html)

Cache catalog vectors only after loading the selected checkpoint and calling `model.eval()`, building them in chunks under `torch.inference_mode()`. PyTorch explicitly notes that inference mode does not set evaluation mode. Engineering implication: bypass and clear caches when training resumes, weights reload, or device/dtype changes; never reuse detached catalog vectors for trainable text encoding. The predictor must reconstruct the same joint embedding architecture and token mapping from that category’s single checkpoint. [PyTorch inference_mode](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.grad_mode.inference_mode.html)
